text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-World Bank to lend Lebanon $65 million for electricity network rehabilitation.
-Parliament Speaker Berri says: "we reject any Syrian troops withdrawal before the an Israeli pullout".
-German enviromental experts arrived in Beirut to examine containers of plastic waste illegally shipped to Beirut.
-The government will win vote of confidence with a large majority.
-Interior Minister Murr reiterates government's ban on demonstrations ahead of a planned strike and demonstration called to by General Confederation of Labour and opposition parties.
-Saudi economic delegation meets Lebanese officials and studies the possibility of investing in Lebanon's reconstruction programme.
-Four unlicensed television stations decided to merge. They called on Berri to back their new application for licensing.
-Opposition MP Wakim said a line should be drawn between interests of Lebanon and Syria.
-Hizbollah guerrillas killed a pro-Israeli intelligence officer of the South Lebanon Army militia.
